site: Shangri-La dune field, Titan, between Dragonfly's landing ellipse and Selk crater (terrain modeled on Cassini data, not real elevation)

frame.description: Local right-handed, y-up frame in meters (Three.js convention). Origin = play-area center. +x = east, +z = south, +y = up. Image columns go with +x, rows with +z; row 0 is the northern edge. Grid north is true north.
frame.projection: Azimuthal equidistant on the Titan sphere R = 2574730 m (IAU mean radius), centered on the origin. Latitudes planetocentric, longitudes EAST (IAU Titan maps use west longitude: origin = 198.551 W).
frame.toLatLon: spherical azimuthal equidistant inverse with x east, y north = -z
frame.heights: All heightmaps store TANGENT-PLANE heights: modeled height above the interdune floor at the origin (Titan has no rover-scale elevation model or usable local datum) minus the curvature drop r^2 / (2R), r = horizontal distance from the origin. The drop is 3.1 m at 4 km, 121 m at 25 km, 1.94 km at 100 km.
frame.azimuthConvention: azimuth_deg is measured from north (local -z), turning toward east (+x). Direction vector = (x: sin(az), z: -cos(az)).

sunAndEarth.note: Titan: Sun only (no Earth block; Saturn is hidden by the haze). Longitude east.

heightmap.source: Generated by this pipeline (seed 2034) from published Cassini measurements; modeled, not measured

slope.source: Computed from the 5 m heights (central differences)

softGround.formula: softness = value / 255 (0 firm ground, 1 loose dune sand); graded, authoritative (see features.softGround)
softGround.source: Generated with the dunes, softened over one pixel

distantTerrain.name: near ring
distantTerrain.hole: Covers the inner grid too; skip or sink the part inside it.
distantTerrain.source: Generated dune field (more seeded rows, 2.2-3.4 km apart, 8-30 km long) and Selk's ejecta; the play-area heights inside

distantTerrain.name: far ring
distantTerrain.hole: Covers the inner grid too; skip or sink the part inside it.
distantTerrain.source: Generated dune field, plus Selk crater at its true position: 80 km across, rim +200 m, floor -150 m, ejecta falling off as (R/r)^3 (Lorenz et al. 2021; IAU)

landing.name: Landing
landing.source: Picked by this pipeline: the flattest firm interdune spot (no sand, 150 m from any dune) in the corridor between Dune 1 and Dune 2. Interdunes are where Dragonfly will land (Lorenz et al. 2021)

duneCrests.description: Linear dunes running roughly west to east, with flat, firm interdune corridors between them. Each line is a dune crest; within zoneRadius_m of a line counts as on the crest. Crests are loose sand (soft ground); the lower flanks and wide plinths are firmer. Dune 1, the smallest, bends to about 80 deg to run along the edge of Selk's ejecta.
duneCrests.source: Modeled on Cassini RADAR dune measurements: west-east orientation, widths 1-2 km, spacing 1-4 km, heights 100-150 m, flank slopes ~10 deg (Radebaugh et al. 2008, Icarus 194; Lorenz et al. 2006, Science 312); plinths and sand-free interdunes near the Dragonfly site (Lorenz et al. 2021, PSJ 2:24). Positions are generated (seed 2034), not mapped: no rover-scale topography of Titan exists.

interdunes.description: Flat, firm, sand-free ground between the dunes. Crossing a dune from one corridor to the next is the Dune crossing milestone. Outlines are closed polygons clipped to the map; the north corridor merges with Selk's ejecta plain.
interdunes.source: Generated with the dunes; sand-free bright interdunes per Lorenz et al. 2021

softGround.description: Dune sand. soft-ground.png is the real mask and is graded: loose crest and upper-flank sand 0.85, lower flanks 0.3-0.6, plinths and interdunes 0, and Dune 1's saddle at most about 0.4. These circles cover only the loose sand (softness >= 0.6), one per 150 m cell (circle area = loose area in the cell), for the circle-based softness rule.
softGround.source: Generated with the dunes. Loose crest sand and firm plinths and interdunes follow Lorenz et al. 2021 (Dragonfly landing site); the Moon's sinkage and slip rules apply

rockyAreas.name: Selk ejecta field
rockyAreas.source: Selk's ejecta blanket is intact, rough and radar-bright, rich in water ice (Lorenz et al. 2021; Cassini RADAR and radiometry); the block field itself is generated
rockyAreas.description: Blocks and rough ground thrown out by the Selk impact, at the outer edge of its ejecta blanket, about 42 km from the rim. Water ice and organics may have mixed here when the crater formed.

viewpoints.name: Dune sea viewpoint
viewpoints.source: Picked by this pipeline: the highest point of Dune 1's crest reached with care in 850-1050 m of driving
viewpoints.note: Looks south across the landing corridor to Dune 2, the branch dune and Dune 3; the crest is 56 m above the landing. Selk's ejecta lies behind, to the north.

samplePatch.name: Bright interdune patch
samplePatch.source: Placed by this pipeline in the landing corridor. Interdunes near the Dragonfly site are bright, sand-free flats (Cassini ISS/VIMS and RADAR; Lorenz et al. 2021)
samplePatch.description: A bright, sand-free interdune flat: firm ground, with organic sand blown in from the dunes. A good first drill site.

crossingRoute.name: Dune 1 saddle crossing
crossingRoute.description: The easiest way over Dune 1: a low saddle in its crest with firmer sand. It leads from the landing corridor to the north side, where Selk's ejecta begins.

fromCorridor.name: Crossing start
fromCorridor.source: Firm interdune ground at the foot of Dune 1's saddle

crestPoint.name: Dune 1 saddle
crestPoint.source: Lowest point of Dune 1's crest near the landing (generated; linear dunes have saddles and junctions along their crests)

toCorridor.name: Crossing end
toCorridor.source: Firm ground north of Dune 1, at the edge of Selk's ejecta

crossingRoute.source: Least-cost route on the 10 m drive grid (slope and loose-sand cost) over the generated terrain

selk.name: Selk
selk.description: Impact crater about 80 km across. Its rim stands only about 200 m above the plains and its floor 100-200 m below; liquid water from the impact may have mixed with organics there. Dragonfly will fly toward it.
selk.source: IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature (Selk, 7.0 N 199.0 W, 80 km); rim height, floor depth and ejecta: Lorenz et al. 2021 (T95 SARTopo, Cassini RADAR)

notes: MODELED terrain: dune sizes, spacing, orientation, plinths, interdune corridors and Selk's size and position follow published Cassini measurements; the exact dunes and blocks are generated (seed 2034). Credits must say 'modeled on Cassini data', never 'real elevation'.
Drive distances are least-cost routes on a 10 m grid avoiding slopes over 18 deg, with a mild cost for loose sand; straight-line distances are also given.

Dune crests stand 22-112 m (Cassini: 100-150 m in Belet, up to ~150 m) on bases 0.75-1.4 km wide plus plinths, kept at the low end so the flanks stay drivable (max slope 17 deg at 5 m; Cassini clinometry gives ~10 deg flanks). The Dune 1 saddle is 24 m high.

Soft ground with the Moon's ground tuning: a reference rover (60 kg, grip 0.55) slips 0.16 on flat loose sand and reaches the 0.2 stuck limit climbing straight up a loose flank steeper than ~14 deg (steepest loose flank: slip 0.21); the crossing route stays at or below 0.08, the route to the Dune sea viewpoint at 0.16. Heavier rovers or weaker wheels sink more.

Play-area center 85 km from Selk's center, on the line from Selk to Dragonfly's landing-ellipse center (67 km south-southeast), about 30 km north of the ellipse's northern edge: on Dragonfly's route to Selk.

Selk's rim is at its true position in the far ring. Seen from the landing it is 2.7 deg below the local horizon (Titan's curvature hides it); from the Dune sea viewpoint it is the skyline toward the north-northwest (-0.3 deg). Titan's haze hides it anyway.
Huygens-like pebbles (Huygens landed on rounded cobbles; Tomasko et al. 2005) appear in the ground texture around the landing only (see texture.json).

horizonFromLanding.note: Index = azimuth in degrees (see frame.azimuthConvention). Includes curvature.
